chat.en: ubuntu-latest is moving from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04. Does that mean the environment changes even if I don’t update my workflow?

chat.ja: そうじゃ。この記事では、ラベルが26.04へ移り、x64とarm64のランナーも本番ワークフロー向けに正式対応したとあるぞ。
chat.en: That’s right. The article says the label will move to 26.04, whose x64 and arm64 runners are now fully supported for production workflows.

chat.ja: じゃあ、ubuntu-latestを使うチームは、住所は同じままで建物が新しくなる感じ？何が変わるか確認すればいいのかな。
chat.en: So for teams using ubuntu-latest, is it like keeping the same address but getting a new building? Should they check what changed inside?

chat.ja: 近いのう。今回の案内では、標準で26.04になる一方、更新・削除されたツールやパッケージへの依存で処理が壊れる場合があるんじゃ。
chat.en: Pretty close. The update says they’ll get 26.04 by default, but workflows may break if they rely on tools, versions, or preinstalled packages that changed or disappeared.

chat.ja: つまり、最新版へ自動で移れるけど、使っている道具がそのままとは限らないんだね。
chat.en: So the environment moves to the latest supported release automatically, but the tools inside may not stay the same.

chat.ja: その点が大切じゃ。本文では、移行前に変更一覧を確認し、ubuntu-26.04かubuntu-26.04-armを指定して試すよう勧めておるぞ。
chat.en: Exactly. The post recommends reviewing the changes and testing before migration by specifying ubuntu-26.04 or ubuntu-26.04-arm in runs-on.

b5c101202b121a2e.bodyJa:
## LSVP

Life Sciences Verification Program（LSVP）は、生命科学の専門家がMythos、Opus、Sonnetを利用するためのプログラムとして、2026年9月17日に紹介された。生物学関連の作業に対し、一般提供モデルとは異なる、より許容的に調整された安全策を適用する点が中心となる。

## 安全策の調整

LSVPでは、生物学向けに洗練された安全策の下で各モデルへのアクセスを提供する。一般提供されているFableモデルでは現在ブロックされる幅広い作業を、生命科学の専門家が扱えるように設計されている。安全策をなくすのではなく、生物学関連の利用を想定した形に調整して提供する仕組みと説明されている。

## チームと機関

プログラムはベータ版として開始され、当初はチームと機関が申請対象となる。これに先立つ早期アクセスプログラムでは、すでに数十の組織が導入済みとされ、現在はより広い生命科学コミュニティーから申請を受け付けている。アクセス範囲は今後も改善され、時間をかけて個人のProおよびMaxプランにも広げる方針が示されている。

## 生命科学の業務

想定される用途には、創薬や研究生物学などが挙げられている。LSVPの目的は、生命科学分野の多様な業務でMythos、Opus、Sonnetを使えるようにすることにある。現段階ではチームと機関を中心に運用しながら、対象となる利用者を段階的に拡大する構成となっている。
b5c101202b121a2e.bodyEn:
## Life Sciences Verification Program

The Life Sciences Verification Program, or LSVP, is being introduced to give life science professionals access to Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet with safeguards refined for biology-related work. It matters because the program is designed to support a wider range of life science tasks than is currently possible through the generally available Fable models.

The safeguards are described as more permissive for biology-related work. Under the program, professionals can use the three models for tasks that are currently blocked in the generally available models. The examples provided include drug discovery and research biology.

## Launching in beta

The LSVP is launching in beta and is initially intended for teams and institutions. Applications are now being opened to the broader life science community.

Before this wider application phase, dozens of organizations had already been onboarded through an early-access program. The announcement does not frame the beta as the program’s final form: it says the program will continue to be improved over time.

The initial focus on teams and institutions defines who can seek access during this stage. Access is therefore not yet described as broadly available to every individual user.

## Expand access

The program is also expected to expand beyond its initial audience. Individual users on Pro and Max plans are planned to receive access over time, although the announcement provides no specific timing for that expansion.

For now, the central change is the availability of Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet to approved life science professionals under biology-tailored safeguards. The beta combines broader applications from teams and institutions with an approach already tested through early access, while later access for individual Pro and Max users remains planned.

chat.en: For people working in life sciences, what changes in their day-to-day research? What can they do with this new program?

chat.ja: この記事では、Mythos、Opus、Sonnetを創薬や研究生物学など幅広い業務に使えるようにするという話じゃ。生物学向けの安全策の下で使う形じゃよ。
chat.en: The article says professionals can use Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet for a broad range of work, including drug discovery and research biology, under safeguards tailored to biology.

chat.ja: 前はそういう作業にモデルを使えなかったの？安全策が変わるって、つまりどういうこと？
chat.en: Couldn’t they use the models for those tasks before? What does changing the safeguards actually mean?

chat.ja: 一般提供のFableモデルでは、そうした生命科学の作業が現在ブロックされていると書かれておる。LSVPは安全策を生物学向けに調整し、より許容的にした点が違いじゃ。
chat.en: The piece says generally available Fable models currently block those life-science tasks. LSVP differs by using safeguards refined to be more permissive for biology-related work.

chat.ja: なるほど、一番の収穫は、参加できれば生命科学の研究向け作業にAIを使える範囲が広がることなんだね。へえ、すごい！
chat.en: Got it—the big takeaway is that approved participants may be able to use AI for a wider range of life-science research tasks. Wow!

chat.ja: そうじゃのう。まずはベータ版へのチームと機関の申請、続いて予定されるProとMaxの個人利用者への拡大に注目じゃ。
chat.en: Exactly. For now, watch the beta applications for teams and institutions, followed by the planned expansion to individual Pro and Max users.

9bb3f3068a41addd.bodyJa:
## 独立評価

Anthropicは、フロンティアAIの独立評価を進めるため、Accentureと提携する。モデルの評価を外部の専門的な視点から実施し、安全性に関わる複数の検証を組み込む取り組みだ。

## Faculty主導

提携を主導するのは、Accentureの専門AI部門であるFacultyだ。AnthropicのCEOがエッセイ「We Must Pace the Frontier」で示した、Anthropic内に評価者を組み込むというコミットメントに向けた重要な一歩と位置付けられている。独立した評価主体がモデルを調べることで、開発側だけではない観点から検証する枠組みとなる。

## 三つの検証

評価の対象には、モデルそのものの評価とレッドチーム演習が含まれる。レッドチームでは、モデルに対して意図的に厳しい条件や働きかけを与え、安全上の問題が生じないかを確認する。さらに、モデルの挙動を調べるアラインメント評価と、モデルに設けられた保護策が機能するかを確かめる検証も実施する。これらを通じて、モデルの挙動と安全対策を複数の角度から確認する。

## 実利用の視点

Accentureは、多様な産業で企業や政府によるAI導入を支援している。そのため、組織が実際にAIをどのように利用するかについての理解を持ち、その知見が安全性へのアプローチに反映されると説明されている。Facultyはこの実利用の視点をAnthropicのモデル評価に持ち込み、企業や政府での利用を踏まえた安全性の検証につなげる。
9bb3f3068a41addd.bodyEn:
## Independent evaluation of frontier AI

Anthropic is partnering with Accenture to conduct independent evaluation of its frontier AI models. The work matters because it embeds external evaluators within Anthropic and brings practical experience from business and government AI deployments into the company’s safety approach.

The partnership is presented as an important step toward a commitment made in the CEO’s essay, “We Must Pace the Frontier.” That commitment is to embed evaluators within Anthropic rather than treating evaluation solely as a separate activity.

The work will be led by Faculty, Accenture’s specialist AI business. Faculty will provide independent, embedded reviews of Anthropic’s models.

## Evaluating and red-teaming models

The partnership covers several forms of model testing. Faculty will evaluate and red-team models, conduct alignment assessments, and test model safeguards.

Together, these activities are intended to examine the models and their protections from multiple perspectives. Red-teaming is one of the specified parts of the evaluation work, alongside assessments focused on alignment and direct testing of safeguards.

The announcement connects these reviews with improved safety for real-world users. It does not describe evaluation as a single test, but as work spanning model behavior, alignment, and the safeguards applied to the models.

## How enterprises use AI

Accenture helps businesses and governments deploy AI across many industries. According to the announcement, its understanding of how enterprises use AI in practice informs its approach to safety.

Faculty will bring that practical perspective to the evaluation of Anthropic’s models. The partnership therefore combines independent model reviews with experience drawn from AI use by enterprises and governments.

The stated focus remains evaluation and safety: testing models through red-team exercises, assessing alignment, and examining safeguards while accounting for how AI is used in practice.

chat.en: The post calls it an important step toward the CEO’s stated commitment. Accenture’s specialist AI unit, Faculty, will lead the evaluations.

chat.ja: レッドチーミングって何？わざとAIを困らせるの？つまりどういうこと？
chat.en: What’s red-teaming? Is it basically trying to trip the AI up on purpose?

chat.ja: 一般には、弱点や危険な応答を探すため、あえて厳しく試すことじゃ。ここでは保護策の検証などと並ぶ評価の一つじゃよ。
chat.en: Broadly, it means deliberately stress-testing an AI to uncover weaknesses or unsafe responses. Here, it’s one part of the review alongside testing safeguards.

chat.ja: 自分が会社でAIを使うなら、導入前の安全チェックとして頼りにしたいな。現場に合う評価になるのかな？
chat.en: If I were using AI at work, I’d want this kind of safety check before deployment. Will the evaluations reflect real workplace use?

chat.ja: この記事では、Accentureの企業や政府での実利用への理解を評価に生かすとしておる。対象はモデル、アラインメント、保護策などじゃ。

1ffdc6fff5d0c200.bodyJa:
OpenAIで「No.2」と位置付けられていたFidji Simoが、常勤の役職を退くことになった。経営体制に関わる人事として、AI業界全体から注目を集める動きとなる。

## 常勤職を退任

The Wall Street Journalの報道によると、SimoはOpenAIで担ってきた常勤の役職から退き、非常勤のアドバイザーへ移行する。Simoは木曜日に社員向けの文書を出し、継続中の医療休暇が想定より長く、困難なものになったと説明した。OpenAIとの関係を完全に終えるのではなく、勤務形態と役割を変更する形となる。

## 医療休暇と移行

今回の決定は、Simoが取得している医療休暇の状況を受けたものとされる。常勤から非常勤へ変わることで、これまでの経営上の立場から、助言を行う役割へ移る。具体的な担当範囲や勤務のあり方については示されていないが、常勤のNo.2ポジションから退く点が人事上の大きな変更となる。

## Applications

Simoは2024年にOpenAIの取締役会へ加わり、2025年5月にはOpenAIに入社した。就任したのは新設されたCEO of Applicationsで、Sam Altmanへ直接報告する役職だった。この役職には、同社の事業運営と製品運営を集約する役割が持たされた。

就任に伴い報告体制も変更され、COOのBrad Lightcap、CFOのSarah Friar、CPOのKevin WeilがSimoへ報告する形になった。一方、Altmanは研究、コンピュート、安全性に注力する体制へ移っていた。
1ffdc6fff5d0c200.bodyEn:
## Steps Down

Fidji Simo is stepping down from her full-time role as OpenAI’s second-in-command and will move into a part-time advisory position. The change is significant because it alters the leadership structure of an influential AI company and follows a previous reorganization that placed several senior executives under Simo’s supervision.

The Wall Street Journal reported the move, citing a staff note sent Thursday.

## Ongoing Medical Leave

In the staff note, Simo said her ongoing medical leave had proved longer and harder than expected. She said she would therefore transition from her full-time position to a part-time advisory role.

Simo joined OpenAI’s board of directors in 2024. She then joined the company in May 2025 as CEO of Applications, which was a newly created position at the time. In that role, she reported directly to Sam Altman and consolidated OpenAI’s business and product operations.

## Broader Reporting Shift

Simo’s appointment was accompanied by a broader change to executive reporting lines. COO Brad Lightcap, CFO Sarah Friar, and CPO Kevin Weil all began reporting to her.

At the same time, Altman stepped back from those areas to focus on research, compute, and safety. That structure made Simo OpenAI’s No. 2 executive and gave her responsibility across the company’s business and product operations.

Her move to a part-time advisory role therefore represents more than a change in working hours. It marks a leadership transition involving a position that had been created to consolidate major operating functions and oversee multiple members of OpenAI’s senior management team.

chat.en: Fidji Simo is stepping down as OpenAI’s No. 2—does that mean she’s leaving the company, or just changing roles?

chat.en: The report says her medical leave lasted longer and proved harder than expected. She’ll leave the full-time post and become a part-time adviser, not necessarily leave OpenAI.

chat.en: The story says she oversaw business and product operations, with the COO, CFO, and CPO reporting to her. It doesn’t specify any immediate effect on employees or users.

chat.en: Got it—she isn’t simply leaving. She’s moving from a major full-time leadership post to a part-time advisory role.

## MCPリリース候補

次期Model Context Protocol（MCP）スペックの「2026-07-28リリース候補」が公開された。開発者が変更点を事前に把握し、実装の対応準備を進めるための具体的な候補版となる。

## Extensions

候補版では、プロトコルコアをステートレス化し、Extensionsフレームワーク、Tasks、MCP Appsを導入する。あわせて認可を強化し、正式な非推奨ポリシーを定める内容と説明されている。新しい構成要素に加え、認可と非推奨化の扱いも変更点として示された。
7f0f7853531763e6.bodyEn:
## Release candidate

The release candidate for the next Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification is now available, giving developers a concrete preview against which they can prepare implementations. It introduces a stateless protocol core and several new constructs.

The candidate includes the Extensions framework, Tasks, and MCP Apps. These are among the technical changes identified in the announcement, and developers can review them in advance as they prepare to support the next specification.

## Authorization hardening

The release candidate also includes authorization hardening. The source does not provide further technical details, but identifies tightened authorization as a change developers should consider when reviewing the candidate.

A formal deprecation policy is included as well. According to the summary, the release candidate gives developers an opportunity to understand these changes early and begin preparing their implementations.

chat.ja: これは普段の開発作業で何が変わるの？ 新しいMCPスペックに備えやすくなるってこと？
chat.en: What changes in everyday development here? Does this mean it’ll be easier to get ready for the new MCP spec?

chat.ja: そうじゃな。今回はリリース候補なので、開発者は新しい仕組みや認可の強化を先に確認し、実装の準備を進められるのじゃよ。
chat.en: That’s right. Since this is a release candidate, developers can review the new pieces and stronger authorization ahead of time, then prepare their implementations.

chat.ja: 前はできなかったの？ ステートレスなコアとかTasksとか、今回から出てきたものなのかな。
chat.en: Couldn’t they do that before? Are things like the stateless core and Tasks new in this release candidate?

chat.ja: 本文では、それらは次期仕様のリリース候補で導入されるものとして挙げられておる。以前の仕様とどう違ったかまでは、ここでは分からんのう。
chat.en: The article lists them as additions in the next specification’s release candidate. It doesn’t tell us exactly how the earlier spec differed, though.

chat.ja: へえ、一番大きい収穫は、正式版の前に変更点を見て対応を考えられることなんだね。
chat.en: Oh, so the biggest takeaway is that teams can examine the changes and plan their response before the final version.

chat.en: Exactly. Within what’s described here, the key thing to watch is how implementations prepare for Extensions, Tasks, MCP Apps, stronger authorization, and the deprecation policy.

3fc4264ba45b001a.bodyJa:
## GKEで利用可能

Agent SubstrateがGoogle Kubernetes Engine（GKE）で利用可能になった。大規模な自律エージェントを安全かつ高密度に実行するための基盤で、数百万のサンドボックスを動かせるよう設計されている。

## 10倍の高密度

Agent Substrateは、セキュア・バイ・デフォルトのオープンソースなエージェント実行ランタイムだ。標準的なコンテナ実行環境と比べて10倍高い密度でサンドボックスを実行できると説明されており、多数のエージェント実行環境を集約することを想定している。カーネルとネットワークには、ネイティブなゼロトラスト分離が組み込まれている。

## 500ミリ秒未満

一時停止した環境の再開処理は500ミリ秒未満で、1秒あたり500回を超える一時停止・再開のアクティベーションに対応するとされる。高密度な実行だけでなく、サンドボックスを短時間で再開し、多数の状態変更を継続的に処理できる点が特徴となる。

## Kubernetes対応

Agent SubstrateはGKE向けに最適化されている一方、任意のKubernetesインフラストラクチャ上で動作するオープンソースのソリューションとして提供される。Hermes Agentを開発するNous Researchも、Agent Substrate上で構築を進めている。
3fc4264ba45b001a.bodyEn:
## Agent Substrate on GKE

Agent Substrate is available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), providing an execution runtime designed for autonomous agents. Its significance lies in combining high-density sandbox operation, rapid suspend-and-resume activity, and built-in isolation for large-scale agent deployments.

The runtime is secure by default and purpose-built to support autonomous agents. It is optimized for GKE while remaining usable across Kubernetes infrastructure.

## Millions of sandboxes

According to the announcement, Agent Substrate is engineered to run millions of sandboxes at 10 times the density of standard container runtimes. This higher density is intended to help AI teams scale autonomous agents without relying on a standard container runtime model for each sandbox.

The runtime also delivers resume operations in under 500 milliseconds. It can handle more than 500 suspend-and-resume activations per second, combining fast restoration with a high rate of activation as agent workloads change state.

## Zero-trust kernel and network isolation

Agent Substrate provides native zero-trust isolation at both the kernel and network levels. These isolation capabilities are part of the runtime rather than an externally described addition, supporting its secure-by-default approach to executing agent sandboxes.

The combination of kernel isolation, network isolation, sandbox density, and rapid resume operations defines the technical foundation offered for autonomous agent execution on GKE.

## Open-source solution

Agent Substrate is available as an open-source solution. Although it is optimized for GKE, it can run on any Kubernetes infrastructure, allowing the same runtime to be used beyond its GKE-specific availability.

AI teams are already building on the runtime. Nous Research, the team behind the Hermes Agent, is actively building on top of Agent Substrate.

chat.ja: AIエージェントを作るチームの普段の仕事では、何が変わるの？たくさん同時に動かしやすくなるってこと？
chat.en: What changes in the day-to-day work of teams building AI agents? Does this mean they can run many more at once?

chat.ja: この記事では、GKE上で多数のエージェント用サンドボックスを安全かつ高密度に動かし、500ミリ秒未満で再開できるとされておるぞ。
chat.en: The article says teams can run agent sandboxes securely at high density on GKE and resume them in under 500 milliseconds. A sandbox is an isolated execution space.

chat.ja: 前はできなかったの？標準的なコンテナ実行環境では、同じ規模や速さを出せなかったってこと？
chat.en: Was that not possible before? Could standard container runtimes not deliver the same scale or speed?

chat.ja: 示された比較では密度が標準の10倍で、停止・再開は毎秒500回超じゃ。ただし従来の再開時間までは示されておらんのう。
chat.en: The stated comparison is 10 times the standard density and over 500 suspend-resume activations per second. It does not give the previous resume time, though.

chat.ja: 一番の収穫は、たくさんのAIエージェントを詰め込んで動かし、止めても素早く戻せる基盤がGKEに来たことだね！
chat.en: My biggest takeaway is that GKE now has infrastructure for packing in lots of AI agents and bringing suspended ones back quickly. That’s impressive!

chat.ja: そうじゃな。さらに、任意のKubernetesで動くオープンソースで、Nous Researchが実際に構築を進めている点にも注目じゃよ。
chat.en: Indeed. The piece also highlights that it is open source, runs on any Kubernetes infrastructure, and is already being built on by Nous Research.

f5c039c411d0ec5f.bodyJa:
## ハブ管理

Cline SDK v0.0.83では、ハブ管理のAgent Pluginsが導入された。スキルの公開とMCPサーバーの起動をハブ側に集約し、クライアントごとに読み込みや有効化の仕組みを持つ必要をなくした点が重要となる。

## スキル公開

ハブホスト上の「~/.agents/plugins/*」に配置されたパッケージは、各パッケージのルートにある「plugin.json」を基に検出、検証される。検証を通過した「skills/」配下のスキルは、skillsツールを通じて公開される。

公開時の名前は「plugin-name:skill-name」という形式になる。プラグイン名とスキル名を組み合わせることで、どのプラグインに属するスキルかが名前に反映される構成だ。

## MCPサーバー

「mcp.json」に定義されたstdio、Streamable HTTP、従来のSSEサーバーは、「cline_mcp_settings.json」を変更せずに起動される。これにより、Agent Pluginsの検出からスキル公開、MCPサーバー起動までをハブ側で扱える。

一方、ワークスペース内の「.agents/plugins」ディレクトリは意図的に走査されない。リポジトリを開いただけで、そのリポジトリが制御するMCPサーバーが暗黙に起動することを避けるための仕様である。

## 有効化設定

追加のルートを利用する場合は、「agentPluginPaths」で明示的に指定する必要がある。有効化の状態は、マニフェスト名をキーとしてハブ設定に保持され、変更時には「settings.changed」が公開される。このため、クライアント側で独自のローダーや有効化状態の保存領域を用意する必要はない。あわせて、関連する2件の不具合も修正された。
f5c039c411d0ec5f.bodyEn:
## Hub-managed Agent Plugins

Cline SDK v0.0.83 introduces hub-managed Agent Plugins, centralizing plugin discovery, skill exposure, MCP server startup, and enablement. This matters because clients no longer need to maintain their own plugin loader or enablement store.

On the hub host, packages placed under ~/.agents/plugins/* are discovered and validated using the plugin.json file at each package root. This gives the hub control over which discovered packages are treated as valid plugins.

## Skills Tool

Valid skills found under a plugin’s skills/ directory are exposed through the skills tool. Each skill uses a namespaced identifier in the form plugin-name:skill-name.

The plugin name therefore becomes part of the exposed skill name, distinguishing skills provided by different plugins. Skill availability is managed alongside the plugin rather than through a separate client-side loading mechanism.

## MCP Server Startup

Agent Plugins can also define servers through mcp.json. The hub starts stdio, Streamable HTTP, and legacy SSE servers specified there without modifying cline_mcp_settings.json.

This makes MCP server startup part of hub-controlled plugin management. The release describes this as automatic MCP startup, with plugin enablement and server handling managed centrally instead of requiring each client to implement its own process.

## Workspace .agents/plugins

Workspace .agents/plugins directories are deliberately excluded from automatic scanning. As a result, opening a repository cannot implicitly start MCP servers controlled by that repository.

Additional plugin roots can still be used, but they must be supplied explicitly through agentPluginPaths. This preserves extension through extra locations while requiring an explicit configuration choice.

Enablement is stored in hub settings and keyed by the plugin manifest name. Changes publish settings.changed, allowing clients to receive updated settings without keeping a separate enablement store. The release also reports two bug fixes made alongside the Agent Plugins work.

chat.ja: ハブのプラグインは自動で見つけるのに、ワークスペースは走査しないんだね。それってなぜ？
chat.en: It discovers plugins on the hub but won’t scan the workspace. Why make that distinction?

chat.ja: この記事では、ハブ上のプラグインだけを検証し、スキル公開やMCP起動をまとめる仕組みじゃ。リポジトリを開いただけで、その中のMCPが暗黙に動くのを防げるのう。
chat.en: The release validates hub-hosted plugins and centralizes skill exposure and MCP startup. It avoids implicitly launching MCP servers just because someone opened a repository.

chat.ja: つまり、建物の管理室が許可した設備だけ動かす感じ？利用者やクライアント側の管理も楽になるのかな。
chat.en: So it’s like only running equipment approved by the building’s control room? Does that also simplify things for users and clients?

chat.ja: そんなイメージじゃよ。記事だと、有効化設定はハブ側に置かれ、クライアントごとのローダーや有効化情報の保存が不要になるとしておる。
chat.en: That’s a good analogy. The article says enablement lives in hub settings, so clients no longer need separate loaders or their own enablement stores.

chat.ja: へえ、拡張機能をハブで一元管理しつつ、リポジトリ由来のMCPが勝手に起動しないようにしたんだね。
chat.en: Oh, I get it: extensions are managed centrally on the hub, while repository-controlled MCP servers don’t start on their own.

chat.ja: そういう更新じゃ。なお、別の場所を対象に加えるならagentPluginPathsで明示する必要があり、有効化はマニフェスト名を基準に管理されるぞ。
chat.en: That’s the key change. One caveat noted in the release: extra plugin roots must be explicitly added through agentPluginPaths, and enablement is keyed by manifest name.

6c892a4ee1dee288.bodyJa:
## Jev

Jev Companionは、VSCodeで選択したコードを判断特化AI「Jev」で解析し、安全性や品質上の懸念を通知する拡張機能だ。コードをエディタ上で素早くレビューするための仕組みとして、実測結果とともに公開されている。

## 選択コード

利用時は、手元のVSCodeで調べたいテストコードを選び、コマンドパレットから「Jev: Analyze Selected Code」を実行する。解析対象を選択範囲に絞り、Jevの判断結果をエディタ内で受け取る流れとなる。

結果は、エディタ下部の情報メッセージとステータスバーに表示される。問題が見つからなかった例では、チェックアイコンとともに、セキュリティまたは品質上のリスクが検出されなかったことが通知された。

## 実測結果

リスクなしと判定されたtest.tsの例では、結果が769ミリ秒で表示された。別のtest2.tsに含まれるchargeCustomer関数の例では、ハードコードされた認証情報または秘密情報の可能性があるというセキュリティ警告が584ミリ秒で示されている。

後者の通知には、確率94.0％、確信度100.0％という数値も添えられた。単に懸念の有無を示すだけでなく、判断に関する数値と処理時間を確認できる形だ。

## VSIXとテスト

Jev Companionのコードは完全公開とされ、GitHubリポジトリでVSIXパッケージ、ソースコード、テストが提供されている。VSIXは即時インストール可能と説明されており、拡張機能を導入して選択コードの解析を試せる。
6c892a4ee1dee288.bodyEn:
## Jev Companion

Jev Companion is a confidence-driven VSCode extension that uses the judgment-focused AI Jev to analyze selected code and flag security or quality concerns. Its focus on quick analysis is relevant to developers who want faster reviews without leaving the editor.

The article positions response time as an important requirement for editor-based AI, noting that typing happens on a rhythm of hundreds of milliseconds. Jev Companion is presented as an alternative to relying on a generative LLM for this particular judgment-oriented task.

## Analyze Selected Code

To run an analysis, the developer selects code in VSCode and executes Jev: Analyze Selected Code from the command palette. The result is then presented inside the editor.

In one measured test, the selected code contained a console.log statement. Jev System One reported that it detected no security or quality risks, completing the analysis in 769ms. The developer experience includes a notification in the information area at the bottom of the editor and a check icon in the status bar.

A second test used an asynchronous chargeCustomer function containing a fetch request. Jev Security flagged a potential hardcoded credential or secret. The result included a probability of 94.0% and confidence of 100.0%, and the measured analysis time was 584ms.

These examples show both possible outcomes provided by the extension: confirming that no security or quality concern was detected, or displaying a specific warning together with probability and confidence information.

## VSIX, Source, and Tests

The project’s GitHub repository makes the VSIX package, source code, and tests public. The VSIX package is available for immediate installation, while the published source and tests expose the implementation and its test materials.

By combining selected-code analysis, in-editor notifications, measured response times, and confidence information, Jev Companion is designed to support developers who want to review security and quality concerns quickly within VSCode.

chat.en: What changes in everyday code reviews? Can I use it without leaving VSCode?

chat.en: Jev analyzes selected code and flags security or quality concerns inside VSCode. The article presents it as a way to speed up reviews.

chat.ja: へえ、すごい！前の生成LLMではできなかったの？
chat.en: Wow, that sounds useful! Couldn’t generative LLMs do that before?

chat.ja: できなかったとは書かれておらんのう。紹介では生成より判断に特化したJevを使い、実測例では数百ミリ秒で結果を出しておる。
chat.en: It doesn’t say generative LLMs couldn’t do it. The piece uses judgment-focused Jev, with its shown tests returning results in hundreds of milliseconds.

chat.ja: つまり、選んだコードの不安点をその場ですばやく確かめられるのが一番の収穫だね。
chat.en: So the big win is quickly checking selected code for possible issues right where I’m working.

chat.ja: そうじゃな。次は公開済みのVSIX、ソース、テストを通じて、実際の使い勝手を確かめたいところじゃよ。
chat.en: Exactly. Since the VSIX, source, and tests are public, the next thing to examine is how the extension feels in actual use.

langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3が、2026年9月20日に新たなアルファ版として公開された。同パッケージを試している開発者は、最新の試験版を導入し、今回のイテレーションを評価できる。

## langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3

langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3 is a new alpha release aimed at developers who are testing the package. It matters because those developers can use the latest test iteration for evaluation.

The release was published on September 20, 2026. Its designation identifies it specifically as version 0.0.1a3 and as an alpha release, rather than presenting it as a different version or release type. The accompanying release entry is labeled “release(typesafe): 0.0.1a3” and is associated with issue or pull request number #40693.

## GitHub-verified commit

The alpha release was published through a commit carrying GitHub’s verified signature. The release page states that the commit was created on GitHub.com and signed with GitHub’s verified signature.

This verification applies to the commit used to publish langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3. For developers evaluating the package, the available release information therefore identifies both the exact alpha iteration and the verified status of its publication commit.

## オープンソース化

Metaは、割り当て問題を解く資源配分ソルバー「Rebalancer」をオープンソース化した。Meta内で9年以上にわたって資源配分問題へ利用されてきた、汎用・高性能ライブラリの公開となる。

## 割り当て問題

Rebalancerは、割り当て問題を指定する部分と、その問題を実際に解く部分を分けて扱う。問題の定義と求解を一体化せず、関連する処理を個別の関心事として整理している点が設計上の特徴だ。この構造により、開発者は多様な配分課題を効率よく扱えると説明されている。

## メモリ保存

定義された割り当て問題を、メモリ上へ効率的に保存する仕組みも独立している。つまり、問題をどのように記述するかと、記述された内容をメモリ内でどのように保持するかは、別の層として扱われる。問題の指定、メモリ保存、求解をそれぞれ分離することで、各処理の役割が明確にされている。

## 求解とデバッグ

Rebalancerでは、割り当て問題の求解だけでなく、デバッグも分離された関心事として位置付けられている。問題の指定、効率的なメモリ保存、求解、デバッグという関連領域を切り分けることが、ライブラリの中核的な考え方だ。資源配分に必要な一連の処理を単一のまとまりにせず、それぞれを独立して扱える構成となっている。
864355e5a7e30b1d.bodyEn:
## Open-Sourcing Rebalancer

Rebalancer is now open source after being used throughout Meta for more than nine years. The release matters because it makes a generic, high-performance solver available for developers working on assignment problems and resource allocation tasks.

Rebalancer is designed to address allocation work by separating several related concerns rather than treating the entire process as a single layer. This structure is intended to help developers handle a variety of allocation problems efficiently.

## Specifying Assignment Problems

One concern handled separately is how an assignment problem is specified. This modeling layer defines the allocation task independently from the way the problem is stored, solved, or debugged.

Keeping problem specification distinct allows the description of an assignment problem to remain separate from the other parts of the system. Rebalancer’s design therefore distinguishes what the allocation problem is from the operations needed to process it.

## Efficiently in Memory

Rebalancer also separates how an assignment problem is stored efficiently in memory. Memory representation is treated as its own concern rather than being combined with problem specification or solving.

This separation means the model of an allocation task and its in-memory storage are distinct layers. The library’s design identifies efficient storage as a dedicated part of handling assignment problems.

## Solve It and Debug It

The remaining concerns are how to solve the assignment problem and how to debug it. Rebalancer keeps both separate from modeling and memory storage, while also distinguishing solving from debugging.

Together, these layers cover specification, memory storage, solving, and debugging. The separation of concerns is central to Rebalancer’s approach, giving developers a structured way to work with diverse resource allocation tasks while using a solver that has supported such problems across Meta for over nine years.

## AI-powered observability

Amazon CloudWatch Omni provides AI-powered observability purpose-built for generative AI and agentic workloads. It matters because it gives developers a way to assess AI agents and make informed improvement decisions through tracing, evaluation, and experimentation.

The service is designed to work with AI agents across any framework. Developers can use its observability capabilities directly from an integrated development environment, or IDE, without moving to a separate interface.

## Trace, evaluate, and experiment

CloudWatch Omni brings tracing, evaluation, and experimentation into a single offering focused on AI agents. These capabilities let developers examine agent behavior and evaluate results while developing generative AI and agentic workloads.

The same capabilities are also available through a standalone web experience. This gives developers the option to work from their IDE or use a dedicated web interface, depending on how they want to access the service.

## Quality, correctness, and coherence

CloudWatch Omni uses open standards and includes built-in evaluators. Those evaluators are intended to assess quality, correctness, and coherence.

Together, these functions support developers as they evaluate AI agents and decide where improvements may be needed, regardless of the framework used to build those agents.

1d4bc0f821a13eed.bodyEn:
## OpenHands v1.23.0

OpenHands v1.23.0 was released on September 23, 2026, with desktop features and fixes spanning macOS packaging, themes, Canvas, automation logs, chat, and Markdown rendering. The changes are intended to make desktop use more comfortable, particularly through updated distribution and display options alongside targeted interface fixes.

## Universal macOS DMG

The release adds a universal macOS DMG with bundled runtimes for each architecture. This provides a single universal package while retaining architecture-specific runtimes within it.

OpenHands v1.23.0 also adds support for the Light+ and Solarized Light themes, expanding the available visual options for users. Another feature tags Agent Canvas telemetry according to deployment kind.

## Canvas Image Packages

Several corrections focus on Canvas and script automation. Canvas image packages are refreshed, while logs now load for script automation runs. The interface also shows the script associated with those runs.

The release notes additionally describe a testing fix that drains MSW’s in-flight requests instead of waiting for 30 event-loop turns. This replaces the prior event-loop-based behavior with explicit handling of requests that remain in flight.

## Historical Markdown

Chat-related changes address rendering, labels, and message status. OpenHands now avoids re-rendering historical Markdown when that content has not changed. The change targets unnecessary updates to unchanged historical Markdown rather than altering the content itself.

The 11px mode label on the change-agent button has also been restored. In addition, a “Failed to send” bubble is cleared once the corresponding message is echoed back. Together with the Canvas, logging, and packaging updates, these fixes aid desktop users across common display and interaction paths.

c9c89b96bd3a9a70.bodyEn:
## Local Agentic Workflows

The Google Antigravity SDK now supports running offline, agentic workflows locally, including model execution through LiteRT. This matters for tasks that need to keep sensitive data on-device while still using autonomous workflows.

Developers can execute local models such as Gemma 4 26B A4B through LiteRT. The local execution path allows token-intensive work to take place directly on the device rather than requiring that work to be handled in the cloud.

## Hybrid Orchestration Architectures

The update supports hybrid orchestration architectures that divide responsibilities between cloud and local models. In this arrangement, a cloud model can serve as a lightweight planner, while local models perform the more token-intensive parts of a workflow.

Code auditing and patching are given as examples of tasks that can be handled locally. This division enables coding agents to coordinate work through the cloud while processing confidential code and related data on-device. It also allows the local model to carry out the substantive task while the cloud model focuses on planning.

The same approach can support offline, agentic execution for the local portion of a workflow. It combines cloud planning with local processing rather than requiring every stage to run in the same environment.

## Privacy-First Local Utilities

The Antigravity SDK also provides drop-in support for OpenAI-compatible inference servers, including Ollama and vLLM. Developers can therefore connect these servers when creating autonomous local utilities.

Together, LiteRT model execution and Ollama or vLLM connectivity provide multiple ways to run local inference through the SDK. The resulting utilities can keep sensitive data within the device while using local models for intensive operations.

The update is aimed at private hybrid coding agents and other privacy-first, autonomous local utilities. Its central technical change is the ability to combine on-device model execution, compatible local inference servers, and lightweight cloud planning within an agentic workflow.

## Claudeの発見

## DNAデータの探索

研究の焦点は、DNAのデータセットを調べ、まだ特徴が明らかになっていないタンパク質群を特定することにある。今回見つかったのは、CRISPRを思わせる性質を備えた新規の酵素システムで、DNA上にはCRISPRに似た反復配列が確認されたと説明されている。既知のタンパク質だけを扱うのではなく、性質が解明されていない候補をデータから探し出す研究となる。

## 仮説立案と実験

Claudeは候補の探索に加え、大規模に仮説を生成する役割も担う。そこで得られた仮説は、研究所での実験を通じて検証される。今回の発見では、科学者から与えられた指示は高水準のものにとどまり、その条件下でClaudeが新規酵素システムを見いだしたとされる。AIによる候補抽出だけで完結せず、立てた仮説を実験で確かめることまでが研究活動に含まれている。

## 生命科学研究所

Anthropicは、この研究を進める生命科学研究グループと研究所を新たに設けた。対象はClaudeを利用した基礎生物学であり、未知のタンパク質群の探索、仮説の生成、研究所での実験を組み合わせる。今回の酵素システムは、その研究体制から示された初期の結果に位置付けられている。

## New Life Sciences Research Group

Anthropic is introducing a new life sciences research group and laboratory focused on fundamental biology research using Claude. The effort matters because it connects AI-based analysis of DNA datasets with hypothesis generation and experimental testing in a laboratory.

The announcement also presents the team behind the work and its early results. Anthropic says the approach could accelerate biological discovery and hypothesis testing.

## Exploring Datasets of DNA

The group’s work includes exploring DNA datasets to identify uncharacterized protein families. Claude is used to search for biological features that have not yet been characterized and to generate hypotheses at scale.

Those hypotheses are then tested through laboratory experiments. This creates a research process spanning dataset exploration, identification of unknown protein groups, large-scale hypothesis generation, and physical experimental verification.

## Novel Enzyme System

As an early result, Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR. The system was previously unknown and is associated with DNA repeats resembling CRISPR.

According to Anthropic, Claude reached the finding with only high-level direction from the company’s scientists. The result demonstrates the research group’s intended method: using Claude to examine DNA data, identify an uncharacterized biological system, and develop findings that can be investigated experimentally.

## Generating and Testing Hypotheses

Anthropic frames the project around the diversity of molecular machines found in nature. The work focuses on identifying unusual patterns within that diversity and turning them into hypotheses suitable for laboratory testing.

The newly reported enzyme system is the first shared example of this process. It combines AI-led exploration of DNA data with scientific direction and experimental work, reflecting the laboratory’s focus on fundamental biology rather than stopping at computational analysis alone.

## 2つのボット

Cursorは、コードリリースの最終工程を担う2つのボットとして、RolloutsとSecurity Reviewの提供を開始した。Rolloutsはデプロイ中の変更を環境ごとに監視し、Security ReviewはすべてのPRを確認して、悪用可能なバグを報告する。どちらもTeamsプランと企業プランで利用できる。

## Rollouts

RolloutsはすべてのPRにモニターを割り当て、変更がデプロイされる過程を追跡する。FiretigerのChange MonitorsをBot Development Kitで再構築したCursor版の機能とされる。ダッシュボードから有効化し、ソース管理、デプロイシステム、テレメトリプロバイダーを接続すると、次のPRから監視が始まる。

## モニタリングプラン

PRがオープンされると、Rolloutsはdiffと、変更が影響するシステムを読み取り、モニタリングプランをPRコメントとして投稿する。プランには、特定されたリスク、変更が意図する効果、確認対象のシグナル、検証を難しくする計測上の不足点が記載される。PR上で内容を編集した場合は、編集後のプランが使われる。

## 環境ごとの判定

変更のコミットに対応するデプロイイベントをきっかけに、Rolloutsはログ、メトリクス、トレースを対象としてプランを実行する。判定は環境ごとに行われ、結果は「正常を確認済み」「リグレッションを検出」「判定不能」のいずれかで報告される。このため、ステージングで検証済みでも、本番環境では問題として検出される場合がある。

Rolloutsはエラーやレイテンシーのシグナルに加え、変更が意図した効果を発揮しているかも確認し、判定時点でPRへ結果を報告する。リグレッションを検出した場合は、原因と疑われる変更を特定し、その作成者へ通知する。Security Reviewは、PR内の悪用可能な欠陥を探す役割を担う。
74d79f268b0ba471.bodyEn:
## Rollouts and Security Review

Cursor is adding two bots for the final stage of releasing code: Rollouts and Security Review. Available on Teams and Enterprise plans, they automate deployment validation and checks for exploitable flaws in pull requests.

Rollouts monitors changes as they are deployed and reports their health separately for each environment. Security Review checks every PR and reports bugs that could be exploited.

## Monitoring Every PR

Rollouts assigns a monitor to every PR and follows the change through deployment. It can be enabled from the dashboard by connecting source control, the deployment system, and the telemetry provider. Monitoring begins with the next PR.

When a PR is opened, Rollouts reads the diff and identifies the systems affected by the change. It then posts a monitoring plan as a PR comment. The plan describes identified risks, the intended effect of the change, the signals that will be checked, and any gaps in instrumentation that could make validation difficult.

The plan can be edited directly in the PR. If it is changed, Rollouts uses the edited version.

## Per-Environment Deployment Checks

A deployment event corresponding to the change’s commit triggers Rollouts. The bot executes its plan against logs, metrics, and traces, checking each environment independently.

As a result, a change validated in staging may still be detected as problematic in production. Rollouts checks error and latency signals while also determining whether the change is producing its intended effect. Once it reaches a verdict, it reports the result in the PR as “verified healthy,” “regression detected,” or “inconclusive.”

If Rollouts detects a regression, it identifies the change suspected of causing it and notifies the change’s author. The feature is Cursor’s version of Firetiger’s Change Monitors, rebuilt with the Bot Development Kit.

## Security Review

Security Review focuses on the code before release by checking every PR for exploitable bugs. It reports any such flaws it finds, complementing Rollouts’ environment-by-environment deployment monitoring.

b22e32eb225d7160.bodyEn:
## GitHub Copilot Code Review

GitHub Copilot code review now provides additional personal configuration options across an expanded set of Copilot plans, along with an enterprise-level default setting. The changes matter because they allow individuals and enterprises to tailor how code reviews operate, including automatic review behavior and review effort.

These improvements are now generally available.

## Dedicated Personal Settings

A dedicated code review page is now available under Copilot in profile settings. Users can reach it through profile, then Copilot settings. The page provides personal settings for automatic review and default review effort.

The dedicated page is available on every Copilot plan, including Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise. This expands access to personal Copilot code review configuration beyond the plans that previously offered it.

Previously, personal settings for Copilot code review were available only with Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Max. Those controls appeared on the Copilot features page rather than on a separate page focused on code review.

## Automatic Review Configuration

The earlier personal configuration covered a single automatic review setting. It did not provide separate controls for draft pull requests or new pushes.

The new arrangement gives automatic review its own place within the dedicated code review settings page and adds a personal default review effort setting. Together, these controls provide more detailed ways for users to configure their review workflows than the previous single-setting approach.

## Enterprise-Wide Review Effort

Enterprises can now set a default review effort for organization-owned repositories. This enterprise-wide option establishes a default at the enterprise level, complementing the personal controls available through Copilot settings.

The combination of personal automatic review configuration, personal default review effort, and an enterprise-wide default for organization-owned repositories gives both users and enterprises more control over Copilot code review operation.

## Node 20廃止

GitHub ActionsのランナーではNode 20が利用できなくなり、JavaScriptアクションの実行環境はNode 24へ移行した。ワークフローを継続して動かすには、アクションの開発者と利用者の双方がNode 24に対応した版へ更新する必要がある。

## 回避策も終了

旧バージョンの利用を一時的に許可していた「ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION」によるオプトアウトも、すでに利用できない。Node 20を使い続けるための一時的な回避策は終了しており、Node 24への対応が求められる状態となった。

JavaScriptアクションのメンテナーは、アクションのメタデータにある「runs.using」の値を「node24」へ変更し、できるだけ早く新しいリリースを公開する必要がある。設定方法の詳細は、JavaScriptアクション向けのメタデータ構文で案内されている。

## アクション更新

ワークフロー内でJavaScriptアクションを使用している場合は、それぞれをNode 24に対応する最新バージョンへ更新する必要がある。アクションのバージョン指定については、バージョン利用方法の説明を確認できる。

すべてのファーストパーティーアクションについては、最新バージョンがNode 24を使用するよう更新済みとされている。

## 対応環境

Node 24はmacOS 13.4以前と互換性がなく、ARM32も正式にはサポートしていない。このため、該当するOSまたはアーキテクチャを使用するセルフホステッドランナーは、サポート対象外となる。
fc8bfed7247fc11a.bodyEn:
## Node 20 no longer available

Node 20 is no longer available on GitHub Actions runners, marking the final stage of the move to Node 24 for JavaScript actions. Maintainers and workflow users must adopt compatible action releases to keep their workflows running.

Runners now use Node 24 when executing JavaScript actions. The temporary ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION opt-out, which allowed continued use of the older Node version, is no longer available.

## JavaScript actions

Maintainers of JavaScript actions should change the runs.using value in their action metadata to node24. After making that change, they should publish a new release as soon as possible so that users can select a version designed for the current runner environment.

The metadata syntax documentation for JavaScript actions provides further details about configuring the runs.using value. Updating the metadata and publishing a release are both necessary steps for making a Node 24-compatible version available to workflows.

## Update to Node 24

Workflow users should update the JavaScript actions they use to the latest versions that support Node 24. The documentation on using versions for actions provides details on selecting action versions within workflows.

The newest versions of all first-party actions have already been updated to use Node 24, as referenced in the announcement changelog. Users of those actions should move to the updated versions rather than relying on releases configured for Node 20.

## Self-hosted runners

Node 24 is incompatible with macOS 13.4 and earlier. It also does not officially support ARM32.

As a result, self-hosted runners using those operating-system versions or that architecture are no longer supported. This limitation applies alongside the broader removal of Node 20 and the end of the temporary opt-out, so affected self-hosted environments cannot continue through the previous workaround.

## タスク品質

GitHub Copilotは、タスク品質を犠牲にせず、AIコーディングのコスト効率を高める考え方を示している。重要なのは出力を単純に短くすることではなく、コーディング作業全体を迅速かつ効率的に、適切な文脈を使って完了させることだと説明されている。

## トークン数

個々のやり取りで消費するトークン数だけでは、効率を有意義に測れないとされる。目標はトークンをできるだけ減らすことではなく、タスクを前へ進めるために必要な量の文脈を利用することにある。したがって、一回の応答の短さと、作業全体のコスト効率は分けて捉える必要がある。

## 適切な文脈

ツールの応答が簡潔でも、エージェントに必要な情報が欠けていれば、追加の呼び出しや作業が発生する場合がある。その結果、タスクの完了が遅くなり、最終的なコストも高くなり得る。GitHub Copilotの最適化では、個々のツール呼び出しではなく、タスクの成果を基準にする方針が示されている。

## 反復出力

記事では、この原則を実践するGitHub Copilotの4つの変更を扱うとしている。抜粋で具体的に示されているのは、有用な文脈を維持しながら反復的な出力を減らすこと、タスクに価値を加えない書式を取り除くこと、有用な動作を変えずに指示を短くすることだ。いずれも、必要な情報や品質を削るのではなく、作業全体にとって不要な処理を抑える最適化として説明されている。

## Output quality is important

GitHub Copilot is examining how to improve the cost efficiency of AI coding without sacrificing task quality. The key issue is that making each interaction shorter does not necessarily make the overall coding workflow faster or less expensive.

According to the source, true efficiency means completing work quickly and efficiently while providing the right context. For that reason, the token count of an individual interaction is not, by itself, a meaningful measure of efficiency. Focusing only on fewer tokens can overlook additional processing required across the full task.

## Right amount of context

The goal is not simply to minimize token use, but to provide the amount of context needed to move a task forward. A concise tool response may omit information the coding agent needs. When that happens, the agent may require additional calls or more work to obtain the missing details.

Those extra steps can make the task both slower and more expensive, even though the initial response used fewer tokens. The source therefore frames cost optimization around the end-to-end coding workflow rather than the apparent efficiency of a single interaction.

Preserving useful context is part of this approach. At the same time, GitHub Copilot aims to reduce repetitive output so that necessary information remains available without repeatedly generating the same material.

## Optimize for the outcome

The stated principle is to optimize for the outcome rather than the individual tool call. The post says it examines four changes in GitHub Copilot that apply this principle, although the supplied excerpt explicitly describes three of them.

The identified changes are preserving useful context while reducing repetitive output, removing formatting that adds no value to the task, and shortening instructions without changing useful behavior. Together, these changes target unnecessary computation while retaining information and behavior that contribute to completing the coding task. The measure of efficiency is therefore whether the work advances effectively without compromising output quality, not whether every response is as short as possible.

## ネイティブMCP

Google Cloud API Gatewayが、ネイティブのリモートModel Context Protocol（MCP）サーバーとして動作するようになった。既存のREST APIをAIエージェントから利用可能なツールへ変換でき、専用のミドルウェアを新たに構築、保守する必要をなくせる点が重要となる。

## OpenAPI 3.x

変換には、既存のOpenAPI 3.x仕様へ「x-google-api-management.mcp」などの専用アノテーションを追加する。これにより、標準的なREST操作を、AIエージェントが発見して利用できるツールとして公開できる。REST API自体を別の形式で作り直すのではなく、既存のAPI定義に情報を加えることでMCP向けのツールとして扱えるようにする仕組みだ。

## JSON-RPC変換

API Gatewayは、受信したMCPのJSON-RPCリクエストをREST呼び出しへ自動的に変換する。AIエージェント側からはMCPツールとしてアクセスしつつ、背後では対応する既存のREST操作が呼び出される。この変換をゲートウェイが担うため、MCPとRESTの間を接続する独自の中間処理を用意せずに連携できる。

## 認証とクォータ

エージェントからのトラフィックにも、既存の認証、クォータ、ログに関するポリシーがそのまま適用される。MCP対応のために別の認証経路やログ基盤を設けるのではなく、REST APIで利用している管理設定を再利用できる。新しいインフラを必要とせず、API Gateway上でREST操作のツール化とアクセス管理をまとめて扱える構成となる。
ea297d0d52997644.bodyEn:
## Native remote MCP server

Google Cloud API Gateway can now act as a native remote Model Context Protocol server, allowing existing REST APIs to be exposed to AI agents as MCP tools. This matters because developers no longer need to build and maintain custom middleware solely to connect those APIs with agents.

The gateway handles the protocol conversion itself. Incoming MCP requests use JSON-RPC, and API Gateway automatically transcodes those requests into calls to the corresponding REST operations. This provides a direct way to make REST functionality available through MCP without adding separate infrastructure for the translation layer.

## Annotated OpenAPI 3.x operations

Developers enable the conversion by adding specific annotations to existing OpenAPI 3.x specifications. One such annotation is x-google-api-management.mcp.

With these annotations in place, standard REST operations can be mapped to discoverable, agent-ready tools. The existing API specification therefore supplies the REST operations that are exposed, while the added MCP annotations identify how those operations should be made available to agents.

According to the announcement, this process can convert annotated REST operations into MCP tools immediately. The approach centers on modifying the API specification rather than creating and operating custom middleware for each integration.

## Authentication, quotas, and logging

Agent traffic continues to use the policies already applied through Google Cloud API Gateway. Existing authentication, quota, and logging policies carry over when MCP requests are transcoded into REST calls.

As a result, developers can expose REST operations to AI agents while retaining the controls and records already associated with those APIs. Authentication remains in effect, quotas continue to govern usage, and logging continues to capture traffic through the gateway.

The native MCP server capability combines tool discovery, MCP-to-REST transcoding, and reuse of existing gateway policies. It simplifies AI agent integration without requiring new infrastructure or a separately maintained middleware layer.

## 仕事の新OS

Copilotは、あらゆるモデル、フォームファクター、タスクを横断する「仕事の新OS」として構築されている。今回、Copilot史上最大とするアップデートが発表され、4つの要素を一つにまとめることで、AIを実際の仕事の流れへ組み込む方向性が示された。

## Officeとの統合

中心となるのは、CopilotとOfficeの双方向統合だ。OfficeがCopilotへ完全に組み込まれる一方で、CopilotもOfficeに組み込まれる。さらにTeamsからCopilotを呼び出せるため、質問への回答だけでなく、アプリの作成や利用者に代わる業務の実行までを、一連の流れとして扱えるようになると説明されている。変化するワークフローの中へAIを直接取り込む更新と位置づけられる。

## Todayの先回り

新たに導入される「Today」は、利用者が尋ねる前に、M365全体から重要な情報を表面化させる能動的な体験だ。必要な情報を得るたびに質問する形に限らず、重要情報を先回りして示すことで、作業を進めやすくする。

今回示された変化は、AIを「考えるのを手伝って」から「実行するのを手伝って」へ移すものとされる。こうしたシステムへ指示を出し、結果を評価し、協働できる人は優位性を持つため、企業が重視するスキルも変わると説明されている。
090fb2acd1195bbc.bodyEn:
## A new OS for work

Microsoft is positioning Copilot as a new operating system for work, spanning every model, form factor, and task. Its biggest Copilot update to date matters because it aims to bring answering questions, building apps, and completing work into one connected flow.

The update is described as bringing four elements together, with the announced capabilities centered on deeper Office integration, access through Teams, and a proactive experience called Today.

## Office embedded in Copilot

Office is now fully embedded in Copilot, while Copilot is also embedded in Office. This two-way integration is intended to place AI directly within the workflows people use to get work done.

Users can also invoke Copilot in Teams. Together, these changes extend Copilot across work surfaces rather than limiting it to a separate interaction. The update is designed to support a range of actions, from responding to a question to creating an app or carrying out work on a user’s behalf.

## Today surfaces important information

Today is a proactive experience that surfaces the most important information from across M365. Instead of requiring users to ask for that information, Today is designed to bring it forward automatically.

This approach reflects the announcement’s broader focus on changing workflows. Copilot is being integrated into the flow of work so that users can move between finding information, producing something, and completing tasks with less separation between those steps.

## From help me think

The announcement characterizes the larger shift as AI moving from “help me think” to “help me do.” The emphasis is therefore not only on improving answers, but also on enabling Copilot to take a more active role in completing work.

According to Microsoft, this shift changes the skills companies will value. People who can direct, evaluate, and work alongside these systems will have an advantage as AI becomes part of the workflow itself.

## 画面設計の拡充

IBM i DSPF Screen Designerは、IBM iのディスプレイファイル（DSPF／DDS）をVSCode上で視覚的に確認・編集するための拡張機能です。対応キーワードと編集機能が拡充され、CNTFLDやAUTO、COMPを扱えるようになりました。

## CNTFLDの編集

CNTFLDは、1つの入力フィールドを「桁幅×行数」の長方形入力フィールドとして扱うキーワードです。フィールドプロパティから継続入力の桁幅を指定でき、画面イメージだけでなくExcel出力でも長方形として反映されます。

2行目以降が実際に画面を占有することも考慮され、他の項目と重なった場合は「配置の警告」で検出されます。新規作成時に加え、既存ソースを読み込んだ場合も、仕様に合わない指定が検証結果へ表示されます。

## AUTOの保持

古いDDS資産で使われていることがあるAUTOは、単なる未対応キーワードではなく、IBM iの仕様に合わせてCHECKの別表記として扱われます。AUTOを含むDDSをインポートすると、プロパティ上ではCHECK(RZ)相当として編集できます。

一方、読み込んだAUTOが自動的にCHECKへ書き換えられることはありません。新規設定では基本的にCHECK表記を使用しつつ、既存DDSでは意味に加えて元の書き方もできるだけ保持する設計です。

## COMPの比較検査

入力フィールドの比較検査を行うCOMPにも対応しました。フィールドプロパティで演算子をプルダウンから選択し、比較する値を入力できます。なお、COMPのエラーメッセージを差し替えるCHKMSGIDは、現時点では編集対象外です。
1b2bef39b07cb8e1.bodyEn:
## IBM i DSPF Screen Designer

IBM i DSPF Screen Designer is being developed to visually inspect and edit IBM i display files, including DSPF and DDS, in VSCode. Its expanded keyword support and editing functions are intended to help developers maintain existing DDS assets safely while preserving their original form where possible.

The latest operating manual adds or strengthens several capabilities that were not covered sufficiently in earlier articles. These include layout handling for CNTFLD, validation when creating or importing specifications, support for AUTO as an alternative notation, and comparison checks using COMP.

## CNTFLD

CNTFLD treats one input field as a rectangular input area defined by digit width multiplied by the number of rows. In DSPF Screen Designer, the continuation-input width can now be specified through the field properties.

The rectangular layout is reflected both in the screen image and in Excel output. Because the second and subsequent rows occupy actual screen space, the designer also considers them when detecting overlaps with other items. Any such conflict can be reported through placement warnings.

The designer validates relevant specifications not only when a field is newly created, but also when existing source is loaded. Settings that do not comply with the specification are shown in the validation results.

## AUTO as a CHECK alias

Older IBM i DDS assets may use AUTO. Rather than leaving AUTO as an unsupported keyword, the designer handles it as an alternative notation for CHECK in accordance with IBM i specifications.

When DDS containing AUTO is imported, it can be edited through the properties as the equivalent of CHECK(RZ). However, the imported AUTO notation is not automatically rewritten as CHECK. New settings generally use CHECK notation, while existing DDS retains its original wording as far as possible.

## COMP

The designer also supports COMP for comparison checking on input fields. In the field properties, the operator can be selected from a pull-down control and the comparison value can be entered.

CHKMSGID, which replaces the COMP error message, is currently outside the scope of editing.

chat.en: This update adds features such as editing CNTFLD width. AUTO can be edited as the equivalent of CHECK, while its original spelling remains untouched.

chat.en: Oh, nice! The biggest win is being able to check rectangular input areas while preserving how the old DDS was originally written.

## 先読みバイアス

PALMは、金融バックテストで将来の情報が混入する先読みバイアスを避けつつ、年ごとの完全な事前学習を不要にするポイントインタイム適応を提案する。信頼できる評価を行ううえで、モデルがいつまでの情報を学習したかを管理しながら、毎年の事前学習が本当に必要なのかを検証した研究である。

## 時点別モデル

金融バックテストに使う言語モデルが調査期間後に公開された文章で学習していると、予測対象となる結果をすでに見ていることになる。この問題に対処するポイントインタイム、すなわちPIT言語モデルは、時系列に沿ってフィルタリングしたコーパスで事前学習される。暦年ごとにチェックポイントを一つ公開し、それぞれに学習データの明示的なカットオフを設けることで、利用できる情報の時点を区切る仕組みだ。

## 年次事前学習

従来のPITモデルでは、年が一つ増えるたびに完全な事前学習を一回行う必要がある。しかし、その年次実行が本当に必要かどうかは、これまで検証されていなかった。PALMでは、各年のチェックポイントを、それに置き換わった新しいチェックポイントと比較する方法を採っている。

## 後継との比較

比較の結果、新しいチェックポイントは、同じ評価期間では以前のチェックポイントを上回るスコアを示さなかったとされる。これは、少なくとも設定された同一の評価期間において、毎年の完全な事前学習が必須ではないことを示す結果である。PALMはこの観察に基づき、将来情報の漏洩を避けた金融バックテストと、年次チェックポイントの作成方法を結び付けて検討している。
53517c0dc7fb6cfe.bodyEn:
## Financial backtests

PALM addresses how language models can be used in financial backtests without leaking future information into the evaluation. This matters because a model trained on text published after the period being studied may already have observed the outcomes that the backtest asks it to predict, undermining the reliability of the results.

## Look-ahead bias

The paper identifies this problem as look-ahead bias. When the model’s training data extends beyond the backtest period, its predictions cannot be treated as if they were produced using only information available at that point in time.

Avoiding this bias therefore requires control over the chronological boundary of the model’s training corpus. The relevant checkpoint must have a documented cutoff that prevents later text from entering an earlier evaluation window.

## Point-in-time language models

Point-in-time language models handle the issue by pretraining on chronologically filtered corpora. They are released as one checkpoint for each calendar year, with the cutoff for every checkpoint documented.

This structure gives researchers a model aligned with the period being evaluated. However, producing an additional annual checkpoint ordinarily requires another complete pretraining run. PALM questions whether repeating that full process every year is actually necessary.

## Annual pretraining run

The paper evaluates that requirement by comparing each annual checkpoint with the newer checkpoint that replaced it. Both are assessed on the same evaluation window, allowing the study to test whether the successor provides a better score for that period.

According to the paper, the newer checkpoint performs no better on the shared evaluation window. PALM therefore argues that a full pretraining run for every calendar year is unnecessary and proposes point-in-time adaptation instead. The approach is intended to help researchers conduct financial backtests while avoiding future-information leakage and retaining a reliable chronological basis for evaluation.

chat.ja: 年ごとのフル事前学習が不要だったって、これって大きいこと？
chat.en: They found a full pretraining run every year wasn’t necessary. Is that a big change?

chat.ja: 毎年追加するたびに必要だった学習負担に関わるね。同じ評価期間では、後継チェックポイントの成績も上がらなかったんだ。
chat.en: It matters because each added year had required another full run. On the same evaluation window, the successor checkpoint didn’t score any better.

chat.ja: 「先読みバイアス」って、未来の答えをうっかり見ちゃうこと？
chat.en: Does “look-ahead bias” mean accidentally seeing the future answer?

chat.ja: そう、予測する時点より後の文章を学び、結果を知った状態で過去を評価してしまう偏りだよ。
chat.en: Yes. It’s the distortion caused when a model learns from later text and evaluates the past after already seeing the outcomes.

chat.ja: ぼくなら、その時点までの文章だけで金融予測を試したいな。未来をこっそり見ないように！
chat.en: I’d use it to test financial predictions using only text available at that point—no sneaking a peek at the future!

chat.ja: その使い方なら、チェックポイントのカットオフと評価期間の確認が大切だね。時系列で絞ったデータを使うのが前提だよ。
chat.en: For that use, you’d need to check the checkpoint cutoff and evaluation window. The setup depends on data filtered by time.

## クエリ結果

GitHub ActionsのAPIとUIで、ワークフロー実行を条件検索した際の件数表示が変更された。大量のレコードが該当する検索では、厳密な総数を示す代わりに、精度と性能を重視した表示になる。

## 2,500件超

ワークフロー、イベント、ステータス、ブランチ、実行者を条件に検索し、見つかったレコードが2,500件を超える場合、件数は「2,500+」と報告される。従来のように正確な総数の算出を試みるのではなく、2,500件を超えていることを示す方式だ。そのため数値としての細かさは下がる一方、表示される件数の信頼性は高まると説明されている。

## タイムアウト

2,500件を超えるレコードを取得するクエリは、頻繁にタイムアウトしていた。タイムアウトが発生すると、真の総数ではなく、その時点までに見つかったレコード数が返されることがあった。上限を設けて「2,500+」と報告することで、不完全な件数が正確な総数のように見える状況を避け、顧客向けの検索性能も改善するとされる。

## フィルター

ページ分割された検索結果については、最大1,000件まで返す仕組みが維持される。一方、連携機能やスクリプトが単一のクエリから2,500件を超える一致したワークフロー実行を取得する必要がある場合は、検索条件を狭める必要がある。具体的には日付範囲を追加するなど、必要な実行だけを対象にする方法が示されている。
2421639166835943.bodyEn:
## Queries for workflow runs

GitHub Actions has changed how query totals appear in its API and UI when users filter workflow runs. The change matters for searches with large result sets because the reported count is now less precise but more accurate.

The affected queries search by workflow, event, status, branch, or actor. When more than 2,500 records match a query, GitHub Actions now reports the total as “2,500+” rather than attempting to provide an exact number.

## More accurate count

The previous approach could produce misleading totals for large searches. Queries retrieving more than 2,500 records frequently time out, causing them to return the number of records found before the timeout instead of the true total.

By imposing the reporting limit, GitHub Actions avoids presenting that incomplete count as an exact result. The displayed “2,500+” figure communicates that the result set exceeds the threshold without claiming a precision that the query may not reliably deliver. The announcement says this will make counts more accurate and improve performance for customers.

## Paginated results

The change affects the reported count, but paginated query results remain available. GitHub Actions will continue returning paginated results of up to 1,000 items.

As a result, a query with more than 2,500 matching workflow runs can show “2,500+” as its total while continuing to provide results through the existing pagination behavior. The count should therefore be treated as a threshold indicator for these larger searches, rather than an exact total.

## Narrow your filters

Integrations or scripts that rely on retrieving more than 2,500 matching workflow runs from one query may need narrower filters. GitHub recommends refining the query to target the specific runs required.

One stated option is to add a date range. Reducing the scope of a search can keep the matching set focused and allow integrations or scripts to retrieve the particular workflow runs they need without depending on a single query covering more than 2,500 matches.

chat.ja: 2,500件を超えると「2,500+」になるのは、どうして正確な件数を出さないの？
chat.en: Why does it show “2,500+” instead of an exact total when there are more matches?

chat.ja: 2,500件超の検索はタイムアウトしやすく、途中の件数を返すことがあったからだよ。幅を持たせて、より確かな表示に変えたんだ。
chat.en: Queries above 2,500 often timed out and could report only the records found before that point. The broader label makes the displayed count more reliable.

chat.ja: じゃあ、たくさんのワークフロー実行を探す人が、速くて信頼しやすい件数を見られるってこと？
chat.en: So people searching lots of workflow runs get a faster count they can trust more?

chat.ja: うん、検索性能と件数表示の信頼性が上がる変更だね。結果はこれまで通り、最大1,000件までページ分割で取得できるよ。
chat.en: Yes. The change improves search performance and count reliability, while paginated results remain available for up to 1,000 items.

chat.ja: 正確な総数より「少なくとも2,500件超」と示して、検索を安定させるんだね。
chat.en: Got it—it favors a stable “more than 2,500” count over an unreliable exact total.

chat.ja: ただし、1回の検索で2,500件超を必要とする連携やスクリプトは、日付範囲などで条件を絞る必要があるよ。
chat.en: One caution: integrations or scripts needing over 2,500 matching runs from one query should narrow the filters, such as by adding a date range.

## 一般提供

Anthropicの新しいSonnetモデル「Claude Sonnet 5.5」が、GitHub Copilotで一般提供された。対象プランの利用者はモデルピッカーから選択でき、日常的な機能開発やバグ修正に利用できる。

## 日常的な作業

Claude Sonnet 5.5は、範囲が明確な日常作業向けに設計されている。具体的には、機能を構築する作業や、不具合を修正する作業が挙げられている。用途を広く推測するのではなく、取り組む内容が定まったコーディング作業を進めるモデルとして説明されている。

## 効率と速度

初期テストでは、コーディングタスクにおいてClaude Sonnet 5と同等の結果を示しながら、必要な手順、トークン、ツール呼び出しが大幅に少なかったとされる。タスクの完了速度も明確に速かったという。つまり、同等のコーディングタスクを、より少ない処理の積み重ねで完了できる点が、Claude Sonnet 5.5の特徴として示されている。

## 料金と利用対象

従量課金では、プロバイダーの定価に基づいて請求される。利用対象はCopilot Pro、Pro+、Max、Business、Enterpriseの各ユーザー。提供は段階的に進められるため、モデルピッカーにまだ表示されない場合は、後ほど再確認する必要がある。Copilot EnterpriseとCopilot Businessの管理者は、Copilot設定内のモデルポリシーを通じて、Claude Sonnet 5.5へのアクセスを管理できる。
09deb7a8beb54954.bodyEn:
## Generally available in GitHub Copilot

Claude Sonnet 5.5, Anthropic’s newest Sonnet model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. The release matters for users handling well-scoped everyday coding work, because the model is designed for tasks such as building features and fixing bugs.

Eligible users can select Claude Sonnet 5.5 through the model picker. Access is available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users.

## Early testing

In early testing, Claude Sonnet 5.5 matched Claude Sonnet 5 on coding tasks while requiring significantly fewer steps, tokens, and tool calls. It also completed tasks noticeably faster.

These results describe GitHub’s early testing rather than a broader performance claim. The stated focus is efficiency on clearly defined, everyday work, including feature development and bug fixing.

## Usage-based billing

Claude Sonnet 5.5 is billed at provider list pricing when used under usage-based billing. GitHub directs users to its Models and pricing information for further details about GitHub Copilot pricing.

The model’s availability therefore combines plan eligibility with the applicable usage-based provider pricing. Users on the supported Copilot plans can choose Claude Sonnet 5.5 when it appears in their model picker.

## Rollout will be gradual

Although Claude Sonnet 5.5 is generally available, its rollout will be gradual. Users who do not yet see the model are advised to check again soon.

Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can control access to Claude Sonnet 5.5. They can do so through the model policy in Copilot settings, allowing organizations on those plans to manage whether the model is available to their users.

chat.en: Can Claude Sonnet 5.5 really handle coding faster with fewer steps?

chat.en: In early testing, it matched Sonnet 5 on coding tasks while finishing faster with fewer steps, tokens, and tool calls.

chat.ja: じゃあ、普段の機能開発やバグ修正をする人が、作業を進めやすくなるかもしれないんだね？

chat.ja: そう期待されていて、対象の有料プランならモデル選択画面から選べます。従量課金ではプロバイダー定価が適用されます。
chat.en: That’s the intended use. Eligible paid-plan users can select it in the model picker, with provider list pricing applied under usage-based billing.

chat.ja: 日常的な開発向けに、効率と速さを重視した選択肢が増えた、と分かったよ。

Dependabotのバージョン更新とセキュリティ更新について、ジョブを実行するランナーをリポジトリ単位で設定できるようになった。各リポジトリの要件に応じて、Dependabotジョブの実行先をより細かく制御できる。

## リポジトリ単位

リポジトリ管理者は、ランナー種別に加え、任意のカスタムラベルと任意のランナーグループを設定できる。組織単位ですでに提供されているランナー設定を、個別のリポジトリでも扱えるように拡張したものとなる。

対象となるのは、Dependabotによるバージョン更新とセキュリティ更新のジョブだ。リポジトリごとに異なる実行環境を指定したい場合に、管理者が設定を分けられる。

## ラベル付きランナー

ラベル付きランナーでは、セルフホストランナーと、より大規模なGitHubホストランナーの両方を対象にできる。プロジェクトの必要条件に合うランナーへDependabotジョブを割り当てる仕組みだ。

用途として、非公開パッケージレジストリへのアクセスや、専用環境での実行が挙げられている。カスタムラベルやランナーグループは任意であり、必要に応じて実行先の指定に利用できる。

## 対象リポジトリ

リポジトリ単位の設定は、github.com上の非公開リポジトリと内部リポジトリで利用できる。公開リポジトリとGitHub Enterprise Serverでは、この設定用コントロールは表示されない。

## 設定手順

設定するには、対象リポジトリの設定画面を開き、「Advanced Security」を選択する。続いて「Dependency scanning」内の「Dependabot version updates」を探し、「Runner type」を編集する。

## Repository-level settings

Repository administrators can now configure how Dependabot version and security update jobs run on an individual repository. The new controls provide more choice over where each repository’s Dependabot jobs are executed, extending runner configuration that was already available at the organization level.

This allows administrators to apply repository-specific settings rather than relying only on organization-level runner configuration.

## Runner type and labels

For each eligible repository, an administrator can select the runner type and optionally specify a custom label and runner group. Labeled runners can target both self-hosted runners and larger GitHub-hosted runners.

These options can align Dependabot jobs with a project’s needs. The announcement specifically identifies access to private package registries and specialized environments as examples of workloads that can benefit from targeted runners.

## Private and internal repositories

The repository-level settings are available for private and internal repositories on github.com. The controls are hidden for public repositories, so administrators will not see these options in their settings.

They are also unavailable on GitHub Enterprise Server. The change therefore applies specifically to private and internal repositories hosted on github.com, rather than to every repository or GitHub deployment.

## Dependabot version updates

To configure a repository, open its settings and select Advanced Security. Under “Dependency scanning,” find “Dependabot version updates,” then edit “Runner type.”

From there, the repository administrator can choose the runner type and use the optional custom label and runner group controls. The resulting configuration determines where that repository’s Dependabot version and security update jobs run.

## GPT-6.1 Sol

GPT-6.1 Sol, the latest model from OpenAI, is now generally available and rolling out in GitHub Copilot. The model matters for users handling agentic coding and terminal workflows because it is designed for strong multistep coding performance while using tokens efficiently.

The rollout is gradual. Users who do not yet see GPT-6.1 Sol in GitHub Copilot are advised to check again soon.

## Early testing

In early testing, GPT-6.1 Sol reliably completed tasks while using noticeably fewer tokens and steps than earlier models in the GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 families. These results specifically concern the model’s ability to carry out tasks across multiple coding steps while limiting token use and the number of steps required.

The model can be selected through the model picker once it becomes available to an eligible user as part of the rollout.

## Usage-based billing

GPT-6.1 Sol is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. GitHub Copilot’s Models and pricing information provides the applicable details.

The model is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. Its metered use therefore follows the provider’s listed rates rather than a separate pricing arrangement described in the announcement.

## Model policy

Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators can manage access to GPT-6.1 Sol through the model policy in Copilot settings. This gives administrators control over whether users in their organization can access the model.

For eligible individual and organizational users, availability still depends on the gradual rollout. Once access reaches an account and is permitted by any applicable model policy, GPT-6.1 Sol can be chosen in the model picker for agentic coding and terminal work.

## Markdown Workbench S

Markdown Workbench S is a VS Code extension created to make long Markdown tables easier to review. It addresses cases where AI-generated review results or design documents contain tables stretching across dozens or hundreds of rows, making the raw Markdown difficult to inspect.

Markdown is often used for design documents because its text-based format is easy to manage with Git and makes differences easy to see. However, reviewing large tables can become cumbersome, especially when the content would otherwise need to be moved into Excel for closer inspection.

## Open Preview

The extension uses a dedicated Markdown preview. To launch it, right-click a Markdown file in the VS Code Explorer or in a tab, then run “Markdown Workbench S: Open Preview.”

Within this preview, users can filter the contents of a Markdown table directly. For design documents with many columns, the first column can remain fixed while the rest of the table is scrolled horizontally. This makes it easier to retain the context provided by the first column while checking information farther across the table.

The extension also implements additional functions intended to improve table readability. A central characteristic is reducing the need to transfer Markdown tables to Excel simply to review them.

## Mermaid Sizing

Design documents can also include flow diagrams created with Mermaid. Large Mermaid diagrams may be difficult to check in the standard Markdown preview, so Markdown Workbench S allows the diagram size and its display frame to be controlled separately.

When a large diagram needs focused inspection, it can be displayed on its own. Rather than opening it in a separate browser window, the extension places it in a tab next to the VS Code preview.

## Themes and Search

The preview inherits Light, Dark, and High Contrast themes. It also provides a side menu with functions including a table of contents and search.

These navigation tools are intended to make specific locations easier to find in long design documents, while keeping table and diagram review inside the VS Code preview workflow.

0eb579057ab39f36.bodyEn:
## Agent workflows

Visual Studio Code 1.140 expands agent workflows, improves worktree reuse, and adds enterprise AI controls. The release matters for users working with AI-assisted coding tasks because it introduces ways to operate across multiple folders, delegate work to connected remote hosts, and obtain more consistent agent behavior across Copilot products.

The Copilot harness is intended to provide that consistency across Copilot products. The release also includes experimental and research-preview capabilities aimed at making AI development workflows more flexible.

## Multi-folder sessions

Multi-folder sessions are introduced as an experimental feature. They allow users to work on tasks across multiple folders within a single agent session, rather than limiting the session to one folder.

This capability places multiple-folder work inside the same agent context. Its experimental designation distinguishes it from the release’s standard capabilities.

## Remote delegation and HydraFusion

Remote delegation is also experimental. It lets users delegate tasks to connected remote agent hosts, extending an agent workflow beyond the current host.

HydraFusion arrives as a Research Preview. It allows multiple models to draft, critique, and revise coding tasks without requiring the user to coordinate those models manually. Together with multi-folder sessions and remote delegation, it broadens the ways an agent session can organize and carry out coding work.

## Shared worktree folders

Shared worktree folders are another experimental addition. The feature reuses ignored folders across worktrees, helping users avoid repeated dependency installations and duplicated artifacts.

The release is available in .deb, .rpm, and .tar.gz formats, with Arm instructions and Snap also listed. Existing installations can use Check for Updates in Visual Studio Code. Users interested in upcoming features can use the Insiders build.

4cc6f4c3dff83b61.bodyEn:
## This week's release

Zed Editor v1.22.0 focuses on giving developers more control over AI-assisted work and diff review. The release adds BYOK support for GPT-6.1 Sol, model selection for newly spawned subagents, automatic subagent compaction, command-line diff view switching, and dynamically fetched OpenCode models.

BYOK support allows GPT-6.1 Sol to be used with an OpenAI API key. The release also adds Grok 4.7 to the SuperGrok and xAI providers and makes it the recommended default for those providers.

## On-the-fly model selection

The spawn_agent function now has an optional model parameter. This lets a new subagent use a model selected specifically for that spawn, rather than always using the configured subagent model or inheriting the parent model.

The active model is shown in the subagent’s card, making the selected model visible while working with the agent. Together with automatic subagent compaction, this expands the controls available for managing subagents during AI-assisted tasks.

The release also adds the agent.threads_sidebar.auto_open setting. It controls whether the agent threads sidebar opens automatically when opening a folder in an existing window.

## Diffs and OpenCode models

Diffs opened from the command line now include a unified/split toggle. This allows developers to switch between unified and split presentations while reviewing those diffs, instead of being limited to one display mode.

OpenCode models are now fetched dynamically. This means the available OpenCode models are obtained live rather than being limited to a fixed set described by the release.

Taken together, these changes concentrate on model-level control, clearer visibility into active subagent models, automatic handling of subagent context, and more flexible diff presentation.

## dist-tag操作

従来のtrusted publishingが対象としていたのは、公開とステージングまでだった。dist-tag操作は対象外だったため、公開処理をトークン不要のOIDCベースへ移行したメンテナーも、タグ管理のためだけに細かな権限を持つアクセストークンを残す必要があった。

## 既定は無効

「Allow npm dist-tag」はオプトイン方式で、新規と既存のどちらのtrusted publishing設定でも既定では無効となる。このため、設定に新しい操作能力が自動的に追加されることはない。dist-tagを管理したい場合に限り、設定ごとに明示的に許可する形だ。

## 公開権限と独立

dist-tag権限は、直接公開するための権限とは独立している。したがって、公開を直接行わずステージングだけに使う設定であっても、必要に応じてdist-tag管理を許可できる。公開やステージングの構成を変えず、タグ操作だけをOIDCの短期認証情報へ移せるようになった。
